entities.text: Bapusaheb Patil vs The City Municipal Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These two petitions are filed by the joint family members feeling aggrieved by the highhandedness of respondent No.1/Corporation in utilizing the private property for formation of the road.
2. The petitioners in these two petitions claim that they are joint owners of property bearing CTS No.2791, along with one Balasaheb Patil.
The grievance of petitioners before this Court is that respondent No.1/Corporation without following any Rules and Regulations highhandedly started forming a road.
This compelled the petitioners to approach the Civil Court by filing an injunction Suit in O.S.No.383/2010.
The petitioners claim inspite of there being a temporary injunction,
respondent
No.1 went ahead with the formation of road and utilized the land owned by the petitioners

. 
3. Present petitioners ancestors along with Balasaheb Patil filed three separate writ petitions seeking NC: 2023:KHC-D:9020 writ of mandamus to respondent No.1-corporation to acquire land and pay compensation.
The learned single Judge rejected all the three writ petitions.
It is only Balasaheb Patil who preferred writ appeal in W.A.No.6132/2011.

The Division Bench of this court negatived the contention raised by the corporation, allowed the writ appeal and directed respondent No.1- corporation to initiate acquisition proceedings and complete within six months including payment of compensation.
Unfortunately, the writ appeal was filed only Balasaheb Patil.
The petitioners ancestors did not choose to assail the order of the learned single Judge.

4. It is brought to the notice of this court that, pursuant to direction issued by Division Bench,
respondent No.1-corportion has initiated acquisition proceedings and to demonstrate its bonafides has deposited admitted amount.
5. If these significant details are looked into, I am not inclined to accede to the arguments advanced by the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9020 counsel for respondent No.1-corporation.

His contention is that petitioners have suffered an order at the hands of the learned single Judge of this court and therefore, orders passed in writ petitions in W.P.Nos.68727-68728/2010 operates as res judicata also cannot be acceded.
Respondent No.1-corporation is not disputing that petitioners land is utilized for formation of road.
6. As regards to Article 31(2) of the Constitution, it is said that it deals with the fundamental right regarding property which is expressed in the clause in negative language.

The provisions of article 31(4) and 31-A and 31-B, though they deprive the expropriated proprietor of his rights provided under (Part-III) of the Constitution, however, they do not in any way affect the ambit of entry 36 and empower the State Legislature to make a law for compulsory acquisition of property without payment of compensation.

In the true sense of the term, emphasis is laid on the words "subject to the provisions of entry 42"
contained in entry 36 and it is contended that exercise of NC: 2023:KHC-D:9020 legislative power under entry 36 is conditional on exercise of power under entry 42,

sentences.text: The incident of the deprivation of property within the meaning of article 300 A of the Constitution, normally occurred, mostly in the context of public purpose.

Clearly,
any law, which deprive the person of his private property will be amenable to judicial review.

In the last 60 years, though the concept of public purpose has been given quite a wide interpretation, nevertheless, the public purpose remains the most important condition in order to invoke article 300-A of the Constitution.
The word property used in article 300-A must be understood in the context in which the sovereign power of eminent domain is exercised by the state and property expropriated.
No abstract principles could be laid.
The phrase deprivation of the property of a person must equally be considered in the fact situation of a case.
Deprivation connotes different concepts.
Article 300-A gets NC: 2023:KHC-D:9020 attracted to an acquisition or taking possession of private property by necessary applications for public purpose.
It is inherent in every sovereign state, by exercising its power of eminent domain to expropriate private property without owners consent.
The question then is whether the owner of the property is entitled to compensation that is just, equal and or indemnification to the owner of the property expropriated.
It is common knowledge that when state exercises its executive power to acquire private property, it is under the land acquisition Act 1894 or similar state laws.

Acquisition being for public purpose, payment of compensation at the prevailing market value as on the date of notification published in the official gazette, is the sine qua non.
7.

In the light of the discussion made supra, if respondent No.1-corporation without having recourse to the provisions of Land Acquisition Act has utilized a private land,
they are bound to compensate lawful owners by initiating acquisition proceedings and pay compensation NC: 2023:KHC-D:9020 therein.

If the Division Bench taking cognizance of the utilization of private property has issued a direction to respondent No.1-corporation insofar as Balasaheb Patil is concerned, the petitioners who are similarly placed cannot be denied their right to seek compensation as they have lost their rights in immovable property.
In that view of the matter, I am of the view that writ petitions deserved to be allowed.
8. Accordingly, the writ petitions are allowed.
9. Respondent No.1-corporation is hereby directed to initiate acquisition proceedings insofar as petitioners portion is concerned and thereafter pay compensation in accordance with law.
